title: Point Blowup Resolution on Arbitrary Regular Surfaces

items.title: Intersection multiplicity of closed subschemes at a point
items.statement: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme, let Y, Z be closed subschemes of X and let p in Y cap Z be a closed point. Assume that Y is integral of dimension one and that the generic point of Y is not contained in Z, so that Y cap Z is supported in the closed points of Y that lie on Z. The local intersection multiplicity of Y and Z at p is m_p(Y cap Z) := length_{O_{X,p}}( O_{Y cap Z, p} ), where O_{Y cap Z, p} = O_{X,p}/(I_Y + I_Z)_p is the local ring at p of the scheme-theoretic intersection. The definition is meaningful: by hypothesis Y cap Z has no one-dimensional component, so its local ring O_{Y cap Z,p} is a zero-dimensional Noetherian local ring, hence has finite length; the value depends only on the local data at p, is unchanged by replacing X by an open neighbourhood of p, and is at least 1. The invariant is the one used for strict transforms: after a blowup one computes m_q(Y' cap Z') in the blown-up ambient scheme at a closed point q over p.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI6
references.locator: Invariant 54.15.2.1, equation (54.15.2.1): m_p(Y cap Z) = length_{O_{X,p}}(O_{Y cap Z,p}); the finiteness discussion following it, Section 54.15.

items.strategy: The support of O_{Y cap Z,p} is the maximal ideal because no component of Y cap Z has dimension one, so the local ring is zero-dimensional and Noetherian; a zero-dimensional Noetherian local ring is Artinian and has a finite composition series (def-composition-series-and-length-of-a-module), so the length is a well-defined natural number. Localization at p and passage to an open neighbourhood of p do not change O_{X,p} or the ideals, so m_p is local. Positivity: the quotient ring is nonzero (p lies in the intersection), so its length is at least one.

items.title: A point blowup drops pairwise intersection multiplicity by at least one
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme, let Y, Z be closed subschemes of X and let p in Y cap Z be a closed point such that Y is integral of dimension one, the generic point of Y is not contained in Z, and the local ring O_{Y,p} is regular. Let pi: X' -> X be the blowup of X in p, with exceptional subscheme E = pi^{-1}(p), and let Y', Z' be the strict transforms of Y and Z. Then: (1) pi restricts to an isomorphism Y' -> Y; (2) Y' meets E in exactly one point q, which is the unique point of Y' over p, and m_q(Y' cap E) = 1; (3) if q also lies on Z', then m_q(Y' cap Z') < m_p(Y cap Z). In particular, blowing up p strictly decreases the intersection multiplicity at every point over p where the strict transforms still meet, and if m_p(Y cap Z) = 1 then Y' and Z' are disjoint over p (the blowup separates the two transversal branches).

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI7
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.3 and its proof (the case computation in the chart A[m/x_1]); complete proof read. The length/valuation dictionary used is the standard length of quotients of a DVR.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI6
references.locator: Invariant 54.15.2.1 used for the two multiplicities compared.

items.strategy: Follow Stacks 54.15.3. Since O_{X,p} -> O_{Y,p} is surjective onto a discrete valuation ring, choose x_1 in the maximal ideal m_p mapping to a uniformizer of O_{Y,p}. On an affine chart Spec A containing p, with defining ideals I for Y and J for Z, shrink so that m = I + (x_1), i.e. V(x_1) cap Y = {p} scheme-theoretically. Then p is an effective Cartier divisor on Y, and since the strict transform of Y is the blowup of Y at p (thm-blowup-closed-immersion-transform-universal), Y' -> Y is an isomorphism. Because m^n is contained in I + (x_1^n), there is a well-defined A-algebra map psi: A[m/x_1] -> A/I sending y/x_1^n to the class of a chosen representative a with y = a x_1^n mod I; it corresponds to a morphism Y cap Spec A -> X' over Spec A restricting to Y' = Y. The image of x_1 cuts out E in the chart, so m_q(Y' cap E) = 1; and if f in J has image in A/I of minimal valuation n = m_p(Y cap Z), then f/x_1 lies in the strict transform ideal J' and psi(f/x_1) = fbar/x_1 has valuation n-1 in the discrete valuation ring O_{Y,p}, whence the length m_q(Y' cap Z') is at most n-1 (length over a DVR is the valuation, additivity of length in the exact sequences of the quotients O_{Y,p}/(x_1^k)).

items.title: The blowup of a one-dimensional integral Noetherian scheme at a closed point is finite
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let Y be an integral Noetherian scheme of dimension one and let p in Y be a closed point. Let beta: Y_1 = Bl_p Y -> Y be the blowup of Y in p. Then beta is proper, finite-type, and locally H-projective, and admits a global closed immersion Y_1 -> Proj_Y Sym(I_p), where I_p is the coherent center ideal; this presentation does not assert a global H-projective immersion into P^N_Y; it restricts to an isomorphism over Y minus {p}; its fibre over p is the projectivized associated graded scheme Proj(gr_{m_p} O_{Y,p}), which is a finite scheme over the residue field kappa(p); consequently beta is quasi-finite and therefore finite. Moreover beta is an isomorphism if and only if O_{Y,p} is regular, equivalently if and only if the maximal ideal m_p is invertible; in the regular case beta_*O_{Y_1} = O_Y.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI4 (Lemma 54.15.1)
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.1 proof: the blowup morphisms are finite because of Varieties, Lemma 33.17.2 (tag 0AB7); complete text retrieved 2026-10-03. The local proof here replaces that finiteness input by proper plus quasi-finite.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0AB7 (Varieties, Lemma 33.17.2)
references.locator: Lemma 33.17.2, condition (1): if f is proper, O_{Y,y} is Noetherian of dimension at most one, and the residue-field extension at every generic point of X over its image is finite or algebraic, then f is finite over a neighbourhood of y. The proof here instead uses proper plus quasi-finite (tag 02LS).

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 02LS (More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.44.1)
references.locator: Proper with finite fibres is equivalent to finite; the library item thm-proper-quasi-finite-is-finite supplies this.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0AGQ (Resolution of Surfaces, Lemma 54.3.1)
references.locator: The fibre of a two-dimensional point blowup is Proj of the associated graded ring, computed via gr_m A = kappa[X,Y]; retrieved 2026-10-03. Here the one-dimensional case is treated by the Hilbert-Samuel computation.

items.strategy: The canonical multiplication quotient Sym(I_p) -> Rees(I_p) yields a global closed immersion Bl_pY -> Proj_Y Sym(I_p), proved on homogeneous degree-zero localization charts and glued over affine base opens. The generic blowup supplier gives local H-projectivity and global properness/finite type. The exceptional fibre is Proj(gr_m A); Hilbert-Samuel degree one makes its Hilbert function eventually a positive constant, so the projective Hilbert polynomial has degree zero and the fibre is finite. Proper plus quasi-finite yields finiteness. Invertibility of the pulled-back center under an isomorphism gives the converse to the Cartier-center isomorphism implication; at a one-dimensional local domain this is exactly regularity. The proof does not import a later coherent-bundle convention or assert arbitrary global H-projectivity.

items.title: The finite normalization of a curve factors through the blowup of a closed point
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let Y be an integral Noetherian scheme of dimension one and let nu: Y^nu -> Y be a finite normalization (a finite birational morphism from a normal one-dimensional scheme; for a reduced curve of finite type over a field this exists and is finite by the normalization theory of curves). Let p in Y be a closed point and let beta: Y_1 = Bl_p Y -> Y be the blowup of Y in p. Then beta is finite, and nu factors uniquely through beta: there is a unique Y-morphism nu_1: Y^nu -> Y_1 with beta o nu_1 = nu. Consequently Y^nu is also the normalization of Y_1, and the finite pushforward beta_* O_{Y_1} is naturally a coherent O_Y-subalgebra of nu_* O_{Y^nu}. If O_{Y,p} is regular then beta is an isomorphism and nu_1 is the original normalization map under the identification Y_1 = Y.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI4
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.1, proof of (4) implies (2)/(3): given a finite resolution X -> Y, the blowup of a singular closed point y admits a factorization X -> Y_i because the ideal sheaf m_y O_X is invertible (local rings of X are discrete valuation rings).

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI5
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.2: the strict transform sequence for Y inside any ambient Noetherian scheme is obtained from the intrinsic blowup sequence.

items.strategy: For a normal one-dimensional Noetherian scheme the local rings are regular: a normal one-dimensional local ring is a discrete valuation ring (normality and regularity agree in dimension one; thm-one-dimensional-regular-local-rings-are-dvrs and the dimension-one case of cor-serre-normality-criterion-two-directions). Hence for every point q of Y^nu lying over p the ideal m_p O_{Y^nu,q} is a nonzero principal ideal of a local ring, and it is the unit ideal at points not over p; therefore the pullback of the ideal sheaf of p is an invertible ideal sheaf on Y^nu. The universal property of the blowup (thm-blowup-universal-property) gives a unique Y-morphism Y^nu -> Y_1; uniqueness is uniqueness of morphisms to the separated Y-scheme Y_1, and existence is exactly the factorization. Finiteness of beta is lem-point-blowup-of-integral-curve-is-finite, so beta_*O_{Y_1} is coherent and the factorization gives the inclusion beta_*O_{Y_1} -> beta_* nu_{1,*}O_{Y^nu} = nu_*O_{Y^nu}. The last clause is the isomorphism criterion of the same lemma.

items.title: Blowing up a non-regular point strictly increases the finite normalization subalgebra
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let Y be an integral Noetherian scheme of dimension one with finite normalization nu: Y^nu -> Y, let p in Y be a closed point that is not a regular point of Y, let beta: Y_1 = Bl_p Y -> Y be the blowup of Y in p, and let nu_1: Y^nu -> Y_1 be the factorization of nu through beta. Then the natural inclusion of coherent O_Y-subalgebras O_Y -> beta_* O_{Y_1} inside nu_* O_{Y^nu} is strict: beta_* O_{Y_1} strictly contains O_Y, with quotient beta_* O_{Y_1}/O_Y a nonzero coherent sheaf of finite length supported exactly at p. More generally, if Y_i -> Y_{i-1} is a blowup at a closed non-regular point and f_i: Y_i -> Y denotes the composite, then f_{i,*}O_{Y_i} strictly contains f_{i-1,*}O_{Y_{i-1}} inside nu_*O_{Y^nu}.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI4 (Lemma 54.15.1)
references.locator: Proof of Lemma 54.15.1: the system f_*O_X contains ... contains f_{2,*}O_{Y_2} contains f_{1,*}O_{Y_1} contains O_Y is a strictly decreasing system of coherent submodules as long as Y_{i-1} is not regular, because each blowup Y_i->Y_{i-1} is not an isomorphism as m_{y_{i-1}} is not invertible; complete text retrieved and read 2026-10-03.

items.strategy: The factorization of the normalization gives O_Y -> beta_*O_{Y_1} -> nu_*O_{Y^nu}; beta is finite, so beta_*O_{Y_1} is coherent, and away from p beta is an isomorphism, so the quotient is supported at p (and has finite length there because p is a closed point of the Noetherian scheme Y). If the inclusion were an equality, then the finite birational morphism beta would satisfy beta_*O_{Y_1} = O_Y; affine-locally this is an injective finite ring map B -> A with the module A equal to B (as the image of 1 spans), so beta is an isomorphism, contradicting the criterion of lem-point-blowup-of-integral-curve-is-finite: beta is an isomorphism only if O_{Y,p} is regular, and here p is non-regular (equivalently m_p is not invertible, so the blowup of the non-invertible ideal m_p is not an isomorphism; a one-dimensional local ring with principal maximal ideal is regular). For the last clause, push the strict inclusion O_{Y_{i-1}} -> (Y_i -> Y_{i-1})_*O_{Y_i} forward along the finite, hence affine and exact on quasi-coherent sheaves, morphism f_{i-1}: on affine base opens the pushforward is exact and faithful restriction of scalars, so the nonzero quotient remains nonzero, giving f_{i-1,*}O_{Y_{i-1}} strictly inside f_{i,*}O_{Y_i}.

items.title: Increasing sequences of coherent subsheaves of a coherent module on a Noetherian scheme stabilize
items.statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme and let F be a coherent O_X-module. If F_1 subset F_2 subset F_3 subset ... is an increasing sequence of coherent O_X-submodules of F, then the sequence stabilizes: there is an index n_0 with F_n = F_{n_0} for every n >= n_0.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI4 (Lemma 54.15.1)
references.locator: Proof of Lemma 54.15.1: the increasing sequence of coherent submodules of the fixed finite modification stabilizes by Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.10.1; retrieved 2026-10-03.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 01Y8 (Lemma 30.10.1)
references.locator: Lemma 30.10.1, statement and proof: quasi-coherent submodules of a coherent module on a Noetherian scheme satisfy the ascending chain condition; a finite affine cover reduces this to module stabilization. Retrieved 2026-10-03.

items.strategy: Choose a finite affine open cover of X by spectra of Noetherian rings (def-locally-noetherian-and-noetherian-scheme). On each chart, the quasi-coherent module F restricts to a finitely generated module over a Noetherian ring (thm-affine-quasi-coherent-equivalence), and a coherent submodule restricts to a finitely generated submodule; an increasing sequence of submodules of a finitely generated module over a Noetherian ring stabilizes at each chart by the ascending chain condition (def-noetherian-module, thm-equivalent-characterizations-of-noetherian-modules). Taking the maximum of the finitely many stabilization indices gives stabilization on every chart; equality of subsheaves of a quasi-coherent sheaf is local on a cover, so the sequence stabilizes globally.

items.title: Regularization of a one-dimensional integral curve with finite normalization by point blowups
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let Y be an integral Noetherian scheme of dimension one whose normalization nu: Y^nu -> Y is finite. Then there exists a finite sequence Y_n -> Y_{n-1} -> ... -> Y_1 -> Y of blowups in closed points such that Y_n is regular. Moreover the sequence may be chosen with every center a non-regular closed point of the preceding curve; then no blowup is an isomorphism, and the increasing sequence of coherent O_Y-subalgebras O_Y subset f_{1,*}O_{Y_1} subset f_{2,*}O_{Y_2} subset ... subset nu_*O_{Y^nu} (f_i: Y_i -> Y the composite) strictly increases at every step, so that termination is exactly Noetherian stabilization of this sequence. No claim is made about normalizations that are not finite, and no higher-dimensional resolution is asserted.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI4
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.1: for a one-dimensional integral Noetherian scheme Y with finite normalization, there is a finite sequence of blowups in closed points ending regular; the proof is the coherent-submodule stabilization argument reproduced item by item here.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0AB7
references.locator: The finiteness input for the blowup morphisms is Varieties, Lemma 33.17.2 in the source; locally it is supplied by Stacks 37.44.1 (tag 02LS).

items.strategy: Suppose Y_{i-1} is not regular. A one-dimensional locally Noetherian scheme is regular if and only if all of its closed points are regular (local rings at non-closed points of a one-dimensional scheme are fields, hence regular), so there is a non-regular closed point p of Y_{i-1}; let Y_i -> Y_{i-1} be the blowup of p. The blowup of an integral scheme in a nonzero ideal is integral (lem-blowup-reduced-integral-under-domain-rees), each Y_i -> Y_{i-1} is finite (lem-point-blowup-of-integral-curve-is-finite), hence each composite f_i is finite, and the normalization factors through every stage (lem-normalization-factors-through-blowup-of-curve-point), so the f_{i,*}O_{Y_i} are coherent O_Y-subalgebras of the coherent module nu_*O_{Y^nu}; by the strict growth lemma each step at a non-regular center strictly increases the subalgebra. If the resulting increasing sequence were to stabilize at a non-regular Y_{i-1}, the strict growth lemma would allow one further strict increase, contradicting stabilization; the sequence is increasing in the coherent nu_*O_{Y^nu} and stabilizes by lem-increasing-sequence-of-coherent-subsheaves-stabilizes, so some stage Y_n is regular, and the construction produces the required finite sequence.

items.title: Regularization of an integral curve on an arbitrary Noetherian ambient scheme
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let X be a Noetherian scheme and let Y subset X be an integral closed subscheme of dimension one whose normalization is finite. Then there exists a finite sequence X_n -> X_{n-1} -> ... -> X_1 -> X of blowups in closed points such that the strict transform of Y in X_n is a regular curve. If the closed points blown up in X are chosen to be the images of the corresponding centers of the intrinsic sequence for Y, the strict transform of Y in X_i is canonically the i-th intrinsic blowup of Y.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI5
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.2 and proof: the intrinsic blowup sequence of Y yields the corresponding sequence of blowups of the ambient Noetherian scheme, because the strict transform is the blowup of the center by Divisors, Lemma 31.34.2 (tag 080E).

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 080E
references.locator: Divisors, Lemma 31.34.2: the strict transform of a closed subscheme under a blowup is the blowup of that subscheme in the inverse image closed subscheme; the library item thm-blowup-closed-immersion-transform-universal supplies this.

items.strategy: Apply the intrinsic regularization theorem to Y, obtaining closed points y_{i-1} of Y_{i-1} with Y_i = Bl_{y_{i-1}} Y_{i-1}. Let X_0 = X and X_i = Bl_{y_{i-1}} X_{i-1}, where y_{i-1} is viewed as a closed point of X_{i-1} via the closed immersion Y_{i-1} -> X_{i-1}. By thm-blowup-closed-immersion-transform-universal the strict transform of Y_{i-1} in X_i is the blowup of Y_{i-1} at y_{i-1}, namely Y_i; induction on i identifies the strict transform of Y in X_n with Y_n, which is regular.

items.title: Point blowups of arbitrary regular surfaces stay regular, with rational exceptional curve over the residue field
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let S be a regular surface: a locally Noetherian scheme of pure dimension two all of whose local rings are regular. Let p in S be a closed point and let pi: S' -> S be the blowup of S in p, with exceptional curve E. Then S' is regular of pure dimension two, E is an effective Cartier divisor on S'; if dim O_{S,p} = 2, E is isomorphic over kappa(p) to the projective line P^1_{kappa(p)}, while if dim O_{S,p} = 1, pi is an isomorphism and E is the reduced point Spec kappa(p), and pi restricts to an isomorphism S' minus E -> S minus {p}. In particular no new singular one-dimensional components are created by the blowup. No smoothness over any base field is asserted: for a non-perfect residue field extension S' can be regular without being smooth over the ground field, and this lemma claims regularity only.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BIA
references.locator: Etale Morphisms, Lemma 41.21.2 (tag 0BIA): criterion for strict normal crossings divisors on locally Noetherian schemes via regularity of scheme-theoretic intersections, used to read off the SNC statement in this pair.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI3
references.locator: Section 54.15 proof of Lemma 54.15.6 uses that the exceptional divisor of a point blowup of a regular surface is a regular curve (Divisors, Lemma 54.3.1, tag 0AGQ).

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0AGQ
references.locator: Lemma 54.3.1, complete statement and proof: blowup of a dimension-two regular local ring, E=P^1 over its residue field; retrieved and inspected 2026-10-03. Regularity follows from the explicit quotient chart argument given here.

items.strategy: Work locally at p. If A = O_{S,p} has dimension one, A is a DVR and its maximal ideal is principal, so the blowup is the identity and the inverse image of p is the reduced Cartier point. In dimension two write m=(x,y) with x,y regular parameters. The x-chart is B=A[T]/(xT-y)=A[y/x]: x is a nonzerodivisor in this quotient because x is prime in A and y is nonzero modulo x, so the x-power-torsion kernel in lem-affine-blowup-algebra-properties is zero. The y-chart is symmetric. A[T] is regular. For a prime Q of A[T] over m containing xT-y, the images of x,y in the cotangent space Q_Q/Q_Q^2 are independent: if Q=mA[T], they are parameters; otherwise choose a lift h(T) of the irreducible polynomial defining Q/mA[T], and x,y,h generate the maximal ideal of the three-dimensional regular local ring A[T]_Q and hence are parameters. The relation xT-y has nonzero linear term, as the coefficient of y is -1. Quotienting a regular local ring by an element of its maximal ideal outside its square remains regular, so each local ring of B above p is regular. Away from p use lem-blowup-isomorphism-off-center. The associated graded ring gr_m A=kappa(p)[X,Y] gives E=P^1_{kappa(p)} in dimension two. In both cases the pullback center ideal is invertible with a nonzerodivisor generator by thm-pullback-center-ideal-invertible, making E effective Cartier. No field smoothness is used.

items.title: Strict normal crossings divisor on a regular surface
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the local factoriality and equivalence arguments. Let S be a regular surface: a locally Noetherian scheme of pure dimension two all of whose local rings are regular. Let D subset S be a reduced curve, i.e. a reduced closed subscheme of pure dimension one, equivalently a reduced effective Cartier divisor on S of pure dimension one. Then D is a strict normal crossings divisor (an SNC divisor) on S if at every closed point p of S one of the following holds: (a) no component of D passes through p; (b) exactly one irreducible component of D passes through p and it is regular at p; (c) exactly two irreducible components pass through p, both are regular at p, and they meet transversally at p, i.e. m_p(Y_1 cap Y_2) = 1 for the two components. Equivalently (Stacks, Lemma 41.21.2, in the locally Noetherian case): D is reduced, every irreducible component of D is regular, and every nonempty scheme-theoretic intersection of two distinct components is a regular scheme of dimension zero, and no three distinct components meet at a point. No smoothness over a ground field is part of the definition; over a non-perfect field the components are regular but need not be smooth.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BIA
references.locator: Etale Morphisms, Lemma 41.21.2 and Definition 41.21.1 (tag 0BIA and preceding definition): a strict normal crossings divisor on a locally Noetherian scheme is an effective Cartier divisor etale-locally of the form V(x_1...x_r) for part of a regular system of parameters, and it is equivalent to reducedness, regular components and regular scheme-theoretic intersections of the expected codimension.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BIB
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.5 and Lemma 54.15.6 (tags 0BIB, 0BIC) use exactly this SNC notion for the final configuration of a resolved curve on a regular surface.

items.strategy: For a closed point lying on the pure-dimensional curve, a height-one component ideal and its proper maximal specialization give local ambient dimension two. Local UFD factorization expresses the radical ideal as a product of distinct prime generators. Regular components correspond to parameter equations, and pairwise transverse intersections correspond to two independent parameters. Require absence of triple intersections separately. At closed points outside the curve the zero-component/unit-ideal case applies, including dimension-one ambient local rings. The converse ambient description retains pure dimension one; a reduced Cartier closed point on a non-Jacobson surface need not be a curve.

items.title: Separation of finitely many curve components by point blowups
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let X be a Noetherian scheme and let Y_1, ..., Y_r subset X be pairwise distinct integral closed subschemes of dimension one, each with finite normalization. Then there exists a finite sequence of blowups of X at closed points such that the strict transforms Y_i' in the final blowup are pairwise disjoint regular curves.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI8
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.4 and proof: reduce to regular Y_i by Lemma 54.15.2, then repeatedly decrease the maximum of m_p(Y_i cap Y_j) using Lemma 54.15.3, and finally separate the curves when the maximum is one.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI7
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.3 supplies both the strict decrease of the maximum multiplicity and the separation of two branches meeting with multiplicity one.

items.strategy: First apply lem-regularization-of-curve-on-noetherian-ambient-by-point-blowups to the components one at a time. A blowup centered at a closed point at which a component is regular restricts to an isomorphism of that component (lem-intersection-multiplicity-drop-under-point-blowup (1)), and a blowup centered away from a component does not meet it; hence once a component has been regularized it remains a regular curve through the later steps. After all components are regular, only finitely many pairs meet, in finitely many closed points. If the maximum intersection multiplicity n = m_p(Y_i cap Y_j) over all pairs and points is greater than 1, blow up all the finitely many points where the maximum is attained; the drop lemma shows that every intersection multiplicity over those points strictly decreases (and the new intersections with the exceptional curves have multiplicity 1), so the maximum strictly decreases. If the maximum is 1, blow up all remaining intersection points; the drop lemma then shows that the two strict transforms no longer meet over the point (the two transversal branches get separated). Both operations are finite in number because the maximum is a positive integer that strictly decreases in the first phase and the finite set of intersection points is emptied in the second; the terminal strict transforms are pairwise disjoint regular curves.

items.title: Embedded strict-normal-crossings resolution of a reduced curve on a regular surface
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let S be a regular surface: a Noetherian scheme of pure dimension two all of whose local rings are regular. Let Z subset S be a reduced curve, i.e. a reduced closed subscheme of pure dimension one, and assume that every irreducible component of Z has finite normalization (this is automatic when Z is of finite type over a field, in particular for a reduced plane curve over a field, by the normalization-finiteness theorem for integral finite-type curves). Then there exists a finite sequence S_n -> S_{n-1} -> ... -> S_1 -> S of blowups of S at closed points such that: (1) every S_i is a regular surface; (2) the inverse image (total transform) Z_n of Z in S_n is an effective Cartier divisor on S_n; and (3) the support of Z_n is a strict normal crossings divisor on S_n in the sense of def-strict-normal-crossings-divisor: every irreducible component (strict transforms of components of Z together with the exceptional curves) is a regular curve, and at every closed point of the support either one component passes or exactly two components pass and meet transversally. Exceptional curves are regular and meet the strict transforms only transversally, so no new singular one-dimensional components are created. The conclusion is SNC support with regular irreducible components; the support itself need not be regular at a crossing; it does NOT assert smoothness of the components over a non-perfect ground field, does not produce a relative SNC divisor with components smooth over a base field, and asserts no resolution of singularities in dimension greater than two.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BIC (Lemma 54.15.6)
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.6 and its complete proof: on a regular surface, finitely many point blowups make the inverse image of a proper closed subscheme with finite-normalization one-dimensional components an effective Cartier divisor supported on a strict normal crossings divisor; retrieved and read in full 2026-10-03.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BIB (Lemma 54.15.5)
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.5: on a regular surface every proper closed subscheme becomes an effective Cartier divisor after finitely many point blowups; in the reduced-curve scope of this item the Cartier property holds from the start and the lemma's auxiliary input Lemma 54.4.1 is not needed (disposed out-of-scope in the coverage record).

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BIA (Lemma 41.21.2)
references.locator: Lemma 41.21.2: the terminal configuration of regular components with transverse pairwise intersections and no triple point is exactly a strict normal crossings divisor; retrieved and read 2026-10-03.

items.strategy: First reduced pure-dimensional curves are Cartier by arbitrary regular-local factoriality under AC. Separate and regularize the finitely many original components; all actual singular/intersection centers have ambient local dimension two, so all introduced exceptional curves are regular, and later point blowups preserve regularity of their strict transforms. The support at this stage can have contact multiplicity greater than one. Blow up all points attaining its finite maximum; regular-component contacts strictly drop and every new exceptional contact is one. This maximum decreases finitely to one. Blow up the finitely many transverse triple points, separating all old directions and introducing only transverse double points. Pullback local equations remain nonzero in blowup fraction charts and hence give Cartier total transforms. This yields SNC support with zero components off support, one or two on support; no smoothness/relative-SNC claim is used.

title: Point Blowup Resolution on Arbitrary Regular Surfaces — Examples

items.title: A node is resolved by one point blowup
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and let k be a field of characteristic different from 2. The nodal plane curve Z = V(y^2 - x^2(x+1)) in S = A^2_k is a reduced curve whose only singular point is the origin, with two regular formal branches having distinct tangent directions and formal intersection multiplicity 1; Z has finite normalization because it is of finite type over k. Blowing up S at the origin once gives a regular surface S_1 with exceptional curve E isomorphic to P^1_k (lem-blowup-of-closed-point-of-regular-surface-is-regular) whose intersections with the strict transform Z' are the two distinct points of E corresponding to the two tangent directions of the branches, each with multiplicity m_q(Z' cap E) = 1; the strict transform Z' is a regular curve and is the normalization of Z. Thus a single point blowup already produces a strict normal crossings support, and the finite sequence of thm-embedded-snc-resolution-of-reduced-curve-on-regular-surface terminates after one step, as proved by the direct chart computation; the original singular node does not satisfy the regular-source hypothesis of the multiplicity drop lemma.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI7 (Lemma 54.15.3)
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.3 gives the affine-chart method for contact with a regular curve. The singular node does not satisfy its regular-source hypothesis; its two formal branches and exceptional contacts are computed directly in Verification steps 2.1 and 3.1.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI8 (Lemma 54.15.4)
references.locator: Once the maximum pairwise multiplicity is one, blowing up the finitely many intersection points separates the curves; retrieved 2026-10-03.

items.strategy: The normal-form embedding proves the node integral with unique singular origin. Construct the two formal branches by the square-root recursion dividing only by two. On the x-chart y=xt the strict transform is x=t^2-1, hence A1_k; the y-chart has s^2(1+ys)=1 and is entirely in the overlap. Exceptional contacts t=+1 and t=-1 are distinct reduced points, each of length one, computed directly. The finite birational map from normal k[t] is the normalization. Its union with the regular exceptional curve is SNC. The formal branches belong to a single global integral curve; the regular-source contact-drop lemma is not applied to the original singular node.

items.title: A cusp: one blowup, the normalization and the delta drop
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and let k be a field of characteristic different from 2 and 3. The cuspidal plane curve Z = V(y^2 - x^3) in A^2_k is reduced with a unique singular point at the origin; it is of finite type over k, so its normalization is finite (thm-normalization-reduced-curve-exists-finite) and is the bijective normalization map A^1_k -> Z, t -> (t^2, t^3). Blowing up the origin once makes the strict transform regular: in the chart y = x t the equation becomes x^2(t^2 - x), so the strict transform is V(t^2 - x), a regular curve meeting the exceptional curve E = V(x) at the single point t = 0 with intersection multiplicity 2; the regular strict transform has curve multiplicity 1 there. Two further point blowups make the total-transform support SNC: the second creates a transverse triple point and the third separates its three tangent directions. The strict transform is precisely the normalization of Z, the multiplicity at the unique point above the origin drops from 2 to 1, and for the projective completion of Z the normalization defect satisfies delta_k = 1 before the blowup and delta_k = 0 after it, in agreement with the general multiplicity formula r m(m-1)/2 with r = 1 and m = 2.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI7
references.locator: Lemma54.15.3 applies to the already regular strict transform and drops its contact with the exceptional curve under subsequent blowup; the first cusp blowup has exceptional contact2, as computed explicitly here, and is not an instance of the regular-source hypothesis before that blowup.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI4
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.1: a finite sequence of point blowups regularizes a one-dimensional scheme with finite normalization; for the cusp one blowup suffices.

items.strategy: In the x-chart y=xt the strict transform is x=t^2, parametrized by t, so it is regular and has curve multiplicity one. Its intersection with E=(x) has length length k[t]_(t)/(t^2)=2, so it is tangent to E and is not yet SNC. Blowing up their intersection, use x=tu: the strict transform becomes u=t, the old exceptional strict transform is u=0, and the new exceptional is t=0; these are three distinct lines through the origin. Blowing up that triple point separates their tangent directions, and each strict transform meets the newest exceptional transversely, giving SNC support after three ambient point blowups. The first strict transform is the normalization: t maps to (t^2,t^3), a finite birational map with regular source. For the projective cubic, the defect is computed directly from k[t]/k[t^2,t^3], with basis the class of t; it is one before and zero after the first blowup. This agrees with lem-blowup-multiplicity-euler-characteristic-drop applied to the reduced projective cubic on P^2_k at its rational cusp, where m=2 and r=1. Subsequent regular-curve point blowups have m=1 and do not change this defect.

items.title: Finite normalization alone does not make a curve regular
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let k be a field of characteristic different from 2 and 3 and let Z = V(y^2 - x^3) in A^2_k be the cuspidal cubic. Its normalization is finite (Z is of finite type over k, thm-normalization-reduced-curve-exists-finite), being the bijective map A^1_k -> Z, t -> (t^2, t^3), but Z is not regular at the origin: the local ring k[x,y]_{(x,y)}/(y^2 - x^3) has dimension one and embedding dimension two, so it is not a discrete valuation ring. This refutes the assertion 'a reduced curve whose normalization is finite is already regular' and shows that the regularization theorem must use blowups: one blowup at the origin makes the strict transform regular, while the normalization map itself is a finite birational morphism that is not an isomorphism over the singular point.

references.title: The Stacks Project, tag 0BI4 (Lemma 54.15.1)
references.locator: Lemma 54.15.1: the finite-normalization condition is one of the equivalent conditions for the existence of a resolving sequence of point blowups; it does not assert regularity of the curve itself. Retrieved and read 2026-10-03.

items.strategy: The unique normal form a(x)+yb(x) embeds the cusp ring as k[t^2,t^3], finite integral over k[x], so the origin has dimension one and independent cotangent classes x,y and is nonregular. The finite normalization k[t] has module generating set {1,t}, not a basis: t^3*1=t^2*t. The same fraction field and UFD normality identify the normalization; the map is an isomorphism off the origin and its origin fibre is supported at one point. The x-chart of the point blowup gives x=t^2 and the y-chart has 1-y*s^3=0 with s invertible, so it lies in the overlap. The whole strict transform is the regular affine line after one blowup. This explicit witness refutes the finite-normalization-implies-regularity claim.
